premises.text: Home robots today are large, expensive, and hard to use; personal robotics needs engaging, affordable, fun robots
premises.evidence_span: take this kind of robots, large, expensive, very difficult to use, and move them into engaging, affordable, and fun to use robots in the home

premises.text: Smartphone and cloud robotics move computation off the robot onto devices you already own, making robots cheaper and dynamically upgradable
premises.evidence_span: smartphone robotics and cloud robotics that takes a computation from the robot into devices you already have, making it much more affordable

premises.text: Ship task-targeted robots that do simple things well and can later unite, instead of Swiss-army robots costing hundreds of thousands
premises.evidence_span: We're going to have a set of robots that are much more targeted at limited set of tasks

premises.text: Shimmy is a dumb hardware shell (motors, speakers, power) with music choreography, tracking, and smarts on phone/cloud
premises.evidence_span: everything that the robot does actually happens on a smartphone app and on the cloud. And the robot is just some motors, high-end speakers, and power

premises.text: Consumer price around $199 (Kickstarter $149) with future app/game and multi-robot concepts
premises.evidence_span: we're able to get it to $199

value.text: Make a robot in every home a reality via affordable personal robotics
value.evidence_span: take the promise of a robot in every home and make it a reality

causal_links.evidence_span: Whenever you have a new phone or a new device on the cloud, your robot becomes smarter
we're able to get it to $199

notes: Large/expensive/hard robots as problem. Smartphone/cloud offload, task-targeted strategy, and Shimmy dumb-robot music/face/clap features folded as one mechanism cascade (§4.1.7). $199/Kickstarter as packaging. Miniaturization/manufacturing trends treated as framing inside affordability claim. Three domains—anti-template: problem, product approach, and price separately revisable.
